data.abstract: Transformer operation and maintenance is very important for the stable operation of the power system, at present, the staff has accumulated a large number of transformer operation and inspection reports, how to effectively use the above data to achieve the prediction and solution of transformer faults is the key to improve the efficiency of transformer operation and maintenance. This paper constructs a transformer intelligent fault diagnosis system that integrates knowledge graph and large language model. Through the fault text preprocessing, knowledge graph construction and the invocation of the large language model to build the transformer intelligent fault diagnosis system, and finally through the entity relationship extraction effect comparison and Q&A system subjective and objective performance evaluation, it is verified that the system can be targeted to solve the information correlation weakness and decision-making generation efficiency in the process of transformer operation and maintenance, and significantly improve the health management level of the transformer.

data.abstract: Accurate transformer health assessment is essential for power system reliability and cost-effective maintenance. Traditional methods relying on single-modality data are limited in accuracy and scope. This paper introduces a multimodal pretrained model that integrates oil chromatographic data, oil temperature data, and core ground current data to generate coherent fault analysis text. Using ResNet-based encoders and a Projector, the model aligns features from different modalities into a unified textual feature space, processed by the LLAMA3-8b large language model. The training process includes feature alignment pre-training and end-to-end fine-tuning to minimize generation loss. Experimental results show that our model outperforms traditional single-modality and previous multimodal approaches in accuracy and relevance of fault diagnosis. This system improves fault detection precision, offers comprehensive transformer health insights, and enables automated diagnostic processes, underscoring the value of multimodal data integration and advanced text generation techniques.

data.abstract: Power transformer failures can cause severe grid disruptions, yet traditional diagnostic methods such as dissolved gas analysis(DGA), infrared thermography, and acoustic sensing each capture only partial fault information, resulting in inconsistent and delayed assessments. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Diagnosis(MMRAGDiag), an on-device transformer fault diagnosis framework that integrates DGA, infrared thermal imaging, acoustic sensing, and manual inspection text through a retrieval-augmented large language model. The system fuses heterogeneous sensor outputs into structured prompts, retrieves relevant maintenance knowledge from a local database, and generates both diagnostic conclusions and maintenance plans in natural language. Implemented entirely on a portable inspection terminal, MM-RAGDiag enables real-time, knowledge-grounded fault detection without cloud connectivity, suitable for bandwidth-limited substations. A proprietary dataset of $\mathbf{1, 0 0 0}$ oil-immersed transformer inspections was constructed to evaluate the framework. Experimental results demonstrate that MM-RAGDiag achieves 97.1 % diagnostic accuracy and a Bilingual Evaluation Understudy-4 score of 72.4, surpassing all unimodal baselines. The ablation and human-Artificial Intelligence comparison studies further confirm that multimodal fusion and retrieval augmentation significantly enhance diagnostic reliability and interpretability, approaching expert-level performance in real-world inspections.

data.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in reasoning, knowledge retrieval, and contextual understanding. However, applying LLMs to fault diagnosis in power communication equipment remains challenging due to the need for highly domain-specific expertise and the high cost of model adaptation. This paper presents a Large Language Model-driven fault diagnosis and analysis system for power communication equipment that combines RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG) with Parameter-Efficient FineTuning (PEFT) to improve domain adaptability, diagnostic accuracy, and interpretability. The system supports intelligent fault identification, root cause analysis, and handling recommendations based on equipment logs, alarm records, and historical maintenance knowledge. In addition, an interactive software interface is provided to enable operators to visualize fault states, query diagnostic reasoning, and interpret suggested actions for on-site decision support.

data.abstract: This paper aims to construct a knowledge graph-enhanced power system fault diagnosis question-answering system based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), addressing challenges in power equipment fault diagnosis such as fragmented data sources, over-reliance on expert experience, low diagnostic accuracy, and insufficient intelligent capabilities. By integrating large language models (LLMs) with domain-specific knowledge bases, the proposed system leverages the open-source framework RAGFlow to retrieve relevant information and generate diagnostic recommendations, thereby enhancing the model’s domain expertise and prediction accuracy to deliver an intelligent solution for power system fault diagnosis. Experimental validation demonstrates that the system achieves significant improvements in diagnostic efficiency and accuracy.
